visualReview.notes: Inspected all seven final portable views against four individually viewed local front, entrance and rear-corner originals. Seven-axis front, rounded corner, gray base, three-bay pediment, semicircular glazed canopy and taller rear mansard remain distinct. Review corrected inward side openings/dormers, curved-corner window occlusion, roof/lightwell gaps and ground masonry joints.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all seven final shared-material views including footprint overlay, plus full front/back views during correction. Stucco, limestone, slate, membrane, painted metal and bronze use shared metric surfaces; glass is local. Flat ground is a material fixture; the portable scene retains independent AHN terrain.

mediumFiReview.notes: All19actual current version2context frames inspected against the clear archive originals. Noon/late,economy/high,full/detail/silhouette and all four forced levels retain facade hierarchy, rounded corner, entrance and mapped/public-AHNroof envelope. No embedded image pixels. Two exact1971HansPeters/Anefo negatives, each explicitly releasedCC0 by its rights holder NationaalArchief, establish the surviving four-storey facade, seven flat axes and rounded corner, central three-bay pediment, rusticated base, balcony and curved entrance hierarchy. These identifying forms match the current model. The model retains the native mapped envelope and original public AHN4roof-height controls (about28.55mNAP versus2.65mstreet), not a roof reconstructed from the1971photo. Later mansard shape/dormers, hidden roofs/courts and modern glazed vestibule remain conservative medium-fi approximations; the archival photographs do not certify those additions. Yellow repaint is supported by Qualla narrative, not inferred from monochrome pixels. Fine sculpture, canopy ironwork and exact restoration are simplified. Accepted at approximate exterior scope; no historic1971restoration or complete current photographic coverage is claimed.
